content.value:
Open CommandOpModeLesson.java.

It extends CommandOpMode and has one method: initialize().

You don't write loop() — the scheduler handles the loop for you.

Put all your setup in initialize(): create subsystems, schedule commands, bind buttons.

It's the only method you'll normally override.

The scheduler starts running right after initialize() returns.

steps.title: Overriding run() when you need a loop

content.value:
If you really need to run code in a loop, you can override run() in CommandOpMode.

But it's strongly advised to do everything in initialize() if possible — schedule commands, set up bindings, and let the scheduler handle every tick.

Override run() only as a last resort.

Start the OpMode.

Nothing happens yet because nothing is scheduled — but it's running. The scheduler loops in the background.

Next you'll learn to feed it commands.
